cues.text: Customers ask: why can my shirt be washed and pressed, but not my pants or jacket? Here is why.
Our shirt press machine is shaped like a shirt. It presses the body, collar, and cuffs in about one minute.
Other clothes do not fit this machine.
Most dress shirts are cotton. Cotton can handle water, high heat, and starch.
Suits and jackets have linings, padding, and stiff layers inside. In water these shrink by different amounts, and you get bubbles and puckers.
Wool pants shrink in water and lose their sharp crease.
Sweaters shrink, stretch, and lose their shape in water.
Dresses are often delicate, and their colors can run in water.
So the easy answer is: shirts are washed and pressed. Almost everything else is dry cleaned, to keep its shape, size, and color.
